images.title: Nothing shared but 1
images.purpose: Show that 96 and 275 share no prime, so 1 is their only common factor and their HCF.
images.composition: Two separate circles with a clear gap between them, one on each side; a single result line sits centred below the gap.
exact_structure: Left circle outlined teal #0072B2, labelled 96, holding exactly 6 primes: 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3.
Right circle outlined amber #E69F00, labelled 275, holding exactly 3 primes: 5, 5, 11.
The circles do not touch or overlap; the gap between them is empty white space.
Centred below the gap, in reddish purple #CC79A7: HCF = 1, and under it the word co-prime.
rejection: the two circles overlapping or touching
the 96 circle not holding five 2s and one 3, or the 275 circle not holding 5, 5, 11
any prime appearing in both circles
images.takeaway: When two numbers share no prime, their only common factor is 1, and they are called co-prime.
images.description: Two separate circles, 96 with primes 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3 and 275 with primes 5, 5, 11, with HCF = 1 and co-prime below.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on numbers whose only common factor is 1.
images.teaching_notes: Look for any prime in both circles; finding none means the HCF is 1.

image_decisions.why: Two separate circles show at a glance that nothing but 1 is common.
